The sources are from known project-related domains, and the license inclusion is transparent. This file adheres to standard AUR packaging practices.

<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The provided PAM configuration file `gxdm-rescue.pam` defines standard session and authentication policies for a display manager in emergency mode. It includes common, legitimate PAM modules such as `pam_loginuid.so`, `pam_keyinit.so`, `pam_env.so`, and `pam_systemd.so`, which are part of the typical Linux PAM stack for session setup and environment initialization. The configuration follows Arch Linux PAM conventions by including `system-login` and `system-auth`, which are standard system policy files.

There are no signs of malicious modifications, such as backdoor triggers, unauthorized network access, or data exfiltration. The use of `pam_systemd.so` ensures integration with systemd for session tracking, which is expected in modern Linux systems. The directive `session required pam_loginuid.so` enforces login UID setup, a security measure. All included modules serve legitimate system-authentication purposes and align with the expected functionality of a display manager in rescue mode.

No obfuscated code, suspicious commands, or unexpected behaviors are present. The file appears to be a standard, properly structured PAM configuration intended for local system authentication in a recovery context.
</details>
